recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-7279 unless the work group later chooses to make deleted-resource ETags mandatory or define a machine-testable conformance rule.
issue_request: FHIR-7279 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core-http. It asked how resource contention is handled when a resource is deleted and then another client updates the previously current version, and the resolution was to add notes to the read and delete operations about returning an ETag for a deleted resource.
initial_application: Git commit e7a0b55a1e6aae358c6571e85a8a9b7f61fc8b21, with subject '#7279 - not about eTag use with deleted resources', added the read and delete notes to source/http.html. Later formatting and HTTP-page updates preserved the substantive rule.
additional_context: source/http.html is the active RESTful API page linked from source/documentation.html. Current read guidance allows a 410 Gone response for a deleted resource and says servers MAY include an ETag on the error response for version contention management; current delete guidance says deleted resources can be brought back to life and servers MAY include an ETag on the delete response. Later Published issues FHIR-23996 and FHIR-25038 support this optional and policy-aware framing, and a 2023 Zulip implementers thread about deleted-resource version ids aligns with response.etag carrying delete version information.
reconciliation: No source changes were made because the requested read/delete ETag notes are already present and strengthening them would be inconsistent with later optionality and access-denied guidance.

related_jiras.note: Softened deleted-resource 410 guidance for security and policy reasons, supporting the current conditional response language.
Clarified that ETag and Last-Modified response headers are generally optional/SHOULD when versioning is supported, supporting the MAY wording retained for deleted-resource ETags.
